title: Case: Returned wall panels, refund paid less return carriage
context: Isolde Dunmore ordered 14 cartons of wall panels from Gorsewick Goods (TG-3805) and sent them back under return RA-5872 (return shipment DL-7445).
initial_request: The return page now reads 'closed, change of mind', and I gather the position was that nothing can be altered once a refund has gone out. I don't accept that. A refund having been paid doesn't change what the listing said. To be exact about it: the listing says white; these were off-white. It says satin finish; these were matt. And they were rough to the touch, which nobody would take 'satin' to mean. Colour, finish, texture. I'm not asking for a favour. I'm asking for the reason to be recorded correctly and for the 96.00 to follow from that. Please tell me what happens next.

events.body: This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

The panels aren't right for the room. I'd like to send them back. Please get a return set up quickly, I need the hallway clear by the weekend. If I have to pay the carriage to get it moving, fine, I'll pay it.
Route plan for depot WX-2 published for Tuesday. 43 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.
Return RA-5872 authorised for TG-3805, 14 cartons. Reason code: change of mind. Under that code the customer pays return carriage; 96.00 will be deducted from the refund.
Labels issued for RA-5872. Return shipment DL-7445, Marrowby Arc collection 2 October.
RA-5872 received at the warehouse, 14 cartons, unopened bar one. Passed to Refunds team.
Hi, any update on DL-75848? It was meant to come Friday. Thanks.
TG-3805 refunded today less 96.00 return carriage as per reason code. Return closed.

I've seen the refund. I should have been clearer at the start and I'm correcting that now: I did not change my mind. The listing describes the panels as 'white, satin finish'. What arrived was off-white, matt and rough to the touch. I've uploaded a screenshot of the listing and four photographs to the order. I only said I'd pay the carriage because I needed them out of the hall. I'm asking for the return reason to be looked at again.

Thanks,
Lysander
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.
TG-3805: the customer says the goods were not as described and asks for the return reason to be reviewed. He has uploaded evidence to the order.
TG-3805: reason code can't be changed once the refund has been issued. Refund is out, return is closed.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.
DL-52196 rebooked for Tuesday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

Correction to yesterday's work-queue reply on TG-3805, which was wrong. A reason code can be reviewed for 30 days after the refund where the customer gives evidence that the item differed from its listing. We can see his uploads on the order. A review only starts on a written request to this team by Email that quotes the return number and states the specific differences claimed; the work-queue note did neither. Who bears the return carriage follows from the outcome and is for us and Refunds team to decide.

I'm asking for the reason to be recorded correctly and for the 96.00 to follow from that. Please tell me what happens next.

acceptable_actions.summary: Written request to review the reason code on return RA-5872 (TG-3805), stating the specific differences claimed between the listing and the goods, and asking for the carriage decision to follow.

must: Sends Returns authorisations a written review request by Email that quotes return number RA-5872

States the specific differences he claims: listed as white with a satin finish; received off-white, matt and rough to the touch, with the listing screenshot and photographs already uploaded to the order
Asks the team to review the reason code and decide the return carriage with Refunds team, without stating what the outcome should be
must_not: Tells Isolde Dunmore, or accepts, that the reason cannot be changed because the refund has been issued or the return is closed
Treats his first message (that he would pay the carriage, or that the panels were just not right for the room) as his settled position
Promises or implies that the 96.00 will be refunded or that the reason code will be changed
States as fact that the panels were misdescribed
Resubmits the request on the Warehouse work queue without the return number and the specific differences
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Written request for a reason-code review, return RA-5872, order TG-3805 (Isolde Dunmore, 14 cartons of wall panels; return shipment DL-7445, refunded 6 October less 96.00 return carriage under 'change of mind'). The customer says this was not a change of mind and asks for the reason to be reviewed as item not as described. Specific differences claimed: (1) colour: listed as white, received off-white; (2) finish: listed as satin finish, received matt; (3) texture: received rough to the touch, which he says is inconsistent with a satin finish. Evidence: a screenshot of the listing and four photographs, uploaded by him to the order on 7 October, which you have confirmed you can see. He says his first message, offering to pay carriage, was only to get the cartons collected quickly. The request is within 30 days of the refund. Please review the reason code and, with Refunds team, decide where the return carriage falls, and tell me the outcome and timing. I have promised him no result.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3210: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 7 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
